source.publication: 2025 IT-511 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Georgia DOR), with Form 500 and Schedule 1 bound in (PDF pages 41-49); Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-7-4-.02(2)
source.section: Subtractions item 1 'Retirement income' (PDF p.21: 'each must qualify on a separate basis. If both spouses qualify, each spouse may claim the amounts above. Income from property that is jointly owned should be allocated to each taxpayer at 50% of the total value'); Retirement Income Exclusion notes (PDF p.24: 'If any item is held jointly, the income or loss should be allocated to each taxpayer at 50%'); Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-7-4-.02(2) ('If property is jointly owned, income derived is allocated to each taxpayer at 50 percent of the total'); Schedule 1 page 2 lines 1-17 and footnote (PDF p.48; 2025GA500.pdf p.8): lines 1-5 earned income, line 6 interest income, line 11 taxable IRA distributions, line 14, line 15, line 16 maximum allowable exclusion 35,000 (62-64) or 65,000 (65 or older), line 17 the lesser of lines 15 and 16; Form 500 Schedule 1 page 1 lines 7a, 7d, 13, 14 (PDF p.47); Form 500 lines 8-16 (booklet PDF pp.16-17: Line 16 'Multiply the amount on Line 15c by 5.19%. Round to nearest dollar.'); rate cite PDF p.9 What's New; standard deduction cite PDF p.16 Line 11

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (person 0) 100,000.00 + interest from a jointly owned account 40,000.00 = 140,000.00. Federal taxable income = 140,000.00 - (standard deduction 31,500.00 + 1,600.00 x 1 aged 65 or older) = 106,900.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Georgia starts from federal AGI). The IRA is in person 0's name and stays with person 0; the joint account's interest is allocated 50% to each spouse (PDF p.21, p.24; 560-7-4-.02(2)): 20,000.00 each. Each spouse qualifies separately with their own maximum (PDF p.21). Schedule 1 page 2 (taxpayer, person 0, age 67: 65,000 branch): line 1 salary and wages 0.00; line 2 other earned income 0.00; line 3 total earned income 0.00; line 4 maximum earned income 5,000.00; line 5 lesser of lines 3 and 4 = 0.00; line 6 interest income 20,000.00; lines 7-10 0.00; line 11 taxable IRA distributions 100,000.00; lines 12-13 0.00; line 14 total of lines 6-13 = 120,000.00; line 15 = 0.00 + 120,000.00 = 120,000.00; line 16 maximum allowable exclusion 65,000.00; line 17 lesser of lines 15 and 16 = 65,000.00. Schedule 1 page 2 (spouse, person 1, age 63: 35,000 branch): lines 1-5 0.00; line 6 interest income 20,000.00; lines 7-13 0.00; line 14 = 20,000.00; line 15 = 0.00 + 20,000.00 = 20,000.00; line 16 maximum allowable exclusion 35,000.00; line 17 lesser of lines 15 and 16 = 20,000.00. Schedule 1 additions lines 1-5 none, line 6 = 0.00. Schedule 1 line 13 total subtractions = line 7a taxpayer retirement income exclusion 65,000.00 + line 7d spouse retirement income exclusion 20,000.00 = 85,000.00; line 14 net adjustments = 0.00 - 85,000.00 = -85,000.00. Form 500 line 8 federal AGI 140,000.00; line 9 = -85,000.00; line 10 Georgia AGI = 140,000.00 - 85,000.00 = 55,000.00. Line 11 standard deduction (married joint) 24,000.00 (the filer takes the federal standard deduction, so must take Georgia's); line 13 = 55,000.00 - 24,000.00 = 31,000.00; line 14 dependent exemption 0 dependents = 0.00; line 15a = 31,000.00; line 15b NOL 0.00; line 15c = 31,000.00. Line 16 tax = 5.19% x 31,000.00 = 1,608.9000 = 1,608.90; the form rounds to the nearest dollar and gives 1,609; expected uses the unrounded formula to the cent. Line 17 Low Income Credit: federal AGI is not under 20,000, so none; no other credits; credits 0.00; state income tax = 1,608.90. For comparison (not the rule): all 40,000.00 to person 0 gives 65,000.00 + 0.00 = 65,000.00 excluded and tax 5.19% x 51,000.00 = 2,646.90; all to person 1 gives 65,000.00 + 35,000.00 = 100,000.00 and tax 5.19% x 16,000.00 = 830.40. Boundary null: person 0's exclusion is at the 65,000 cap, person 1's below the 35,000 cap.
